summary: Ephemeral heartbeat jitter and reservation fragmentation triggering autoscaler misclassification and throughput degradation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (VectorQ AI, dedicated tenant) reports repeated midday throughput drops over the last 48h on their reserved pool in us-west-2. Symptoms: p99 latency spike to 3-6s for short-text streaming requests, sudden queue length increase on tenant route, and autoscaler failing to add capacity for ~6-8 minute windows. Heartbeat flapping from tenant slots and short-lived slot reservations observed in metrics.

Impact:
- Customer reports user-facing latency spikes and occasional request failures (502/524) during peaks.
- Affects ~30% of their production routes (small-streams, high qps) reducing effective throughput by ~40% during events.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) assigned to VectorQ AI
- Region: us-west-2 primary, fallback to us-east-1
- Models: redwood-open-7b (main), rw-compat-small-chat for low-cost routes
- Serving runtime v2.6.1, scheduler v1.9.3, autoscaler v3.0.0-beta

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant sends a burst of many short-stream requests from many client IPs (common for mobile fanout).
2) Scheduler creates many ephemeral reservations / heartbeats for small streams; heartbeats show jitter (intermittent delays of 200-800ms).
3) Slot allocation becomes fragmented: many slots marked live but underutilized and with short-lived KV caches.
4) Autoscaler moving-average window interprets noisy signal as sustained warm tail -> chooses conservative scale policy but cannot consolidate fragmented slots.
5) New incoming requests queue and are routed to fallback lower-capacity nodes or throttled, causing p99 latency and occasional 502/524s.

Observed logs/metrics (relevant extracts):
- Scheduler heartbeat latency: median 35ms, 95th 420ms, 99th 760ms during event windows.
- Slot churn metric (slots/sec for tenant): baseline 0.2, spike to 4.6 during bursts.
- Autoscaler decision log: at 2026-03-13T16:18Z: "no-scale (fragmented), score=0.42, trend=unstable" then at 16:26Z: "deferred-add -> no-op".
- GPU utilization: pool avg 62% but many GPUs show <10% per-slot utilization due to many small isolated batches.
- Queue length: route qlen from 0->85 in <90s.

Investigation notes:
- Correlated tenant traffic with customer-side client releases pushing many concurrent short streams (mobile fanout pattern).
- Detailed trace shows high rate of short-lived connections; prefetcher on client side sets concurrency=16 leading to many tiny streams.
- There is measurable scheduler heartbeat jitter between sidecar and scheduler during these windows; network path introduces 100-800ms variance for many ephemeral connections.
- Autoscaler currently uses a 5-minute moving average with conservative thresholds; fragmentation causes it to undercount effective headroom and delay provisioning.
- No evidence of underlying GPU hardware faults. NVLink/PCIe metrics normal outside short bursts.

Hypothesis:
Primary: Heartbeat jitter + high fanout of short streams produces slot fragmentation (many small reservations with cold KV caches). The autoscaler misclassifies the signal as non-actionable because the per-GPU aggregate utilization masks per-slot underutilization and fragmentation. Combined effect -> transient effective GPU shortage and queuing. Secondary: client prefetch/concurrency settings exacerbate the problem.

Mitigation / temporary workarounds applied:
- Support recommended customer reduce client prefetch concurrency from 16 -> 4 for short-stream routes. Customer applied change at 2026-03-13T18:10Z; immediate reduction in slot churn and queue growth observed.
- Applied temporary increase to autoscaler sensitivity for the tenant's pool (lowered add threshold) at 2026-03-13T18:35Z which allowed a one-time add of 2 GPUs and cleared queues.
- Enabled short-lived slot coalescing (experimental switch) for the tenant to aggregate small streams on fewer GPUs for 2 hours as a pilot.

Root cause candidate fixes (engineering):
- Scheduler: implement heartbeat coalescing and tolerance window to avoid marking many ephemeral slots live when bursts are short-lived.
- Autoscaler: add fragmentation-aware metric (slot_churn adjusted) instead of raw aggregate GPU utilization; use per-slot utilization percentiles when evaluating adds.
- Serving runtime: improve small-batch consolidation and KV cache warmup prioritization for tiny streams.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering owner (Ravi Shah) to open runtime/scheduler PRs to add heartbeat coalescing and fragmentation signals (ETA: 7 days).
- Product/SRE to create an autoscaler tweak experiment for dedicated pools to detect high churn patterns and scale faster (ETA: 3 days for experiment config).
- Customer success to coordinate with VectorQ to roll back concurrency settings in a controlled way and monitor for regressions.
- Follow-up runbook addition: detect high slot_churn + low per-slot-utilization -> run mitigation (coalesce, temporarily relax autoscale thresholds).

Resolution notes (temporary):
- Customer reverted client prefetch to 4 and enabled coalescing pilot; throughput stabilized and p99 dropped to acceptable range within 10-15 minutes.
- Engineering changes are required to prevent recurrence under similar fanout patterns.

References/log links:
- Scheduler heartbeat heatmap: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/heartbeats/tenant-553780
- Autoscaler decision trace: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/0b8f3c3a-autoscale-20260313
- Customer support slack: https://slack.redwood.ai/support/p12345
